cards.headline: The song ends by indicting Kendrick himself
cards.snippet: On "Auntie Diaries," from his 2022 album Mr. Morale & the Big Steppers, Kendrick Lamar ends with a story about an earlier show. He had invited a white female fan on stage to perform his song with him, then disapproved when she said the n-word as part of it. He tells this in third person and criticizes himself as a hypocrite. That ending leaves listeners to question his own use of the f-slur earlier in the song.
cards.context: The closing twist reframes his own use of the f-slur earlier in the song.

cards.headline: The fan on stage was at Hangout Festival 2018
cards.snippet: In 2018, at the Hangout festival, Kendrick Lamar brought a white female fan on stage to rap one of his verses. Variety says she used the n-word and was booed, and Lamar gently but sternly lectured her onstage. The review says he has apparently come to think twice about what he said. Years later, on "Auntie Diaries" (2022), he points a finger at himself over that moment.
cards.context: Variety reads the song as a reflection on that moment.

cards.headline: Kendrick's speech and Auntie Diaries live at Paycom Arena
cards.snippet: Recorded July 19, 2022 at The Paycom Arena in Oklahoma City, this set pairs a spoken speech with the song, so it plays as a stage moment rather than a studio track. One listener: "He lost the beat at the end there but finished strong, true performance"
cards.context: Live recording uploaded by Norman Music Archive.

cards.headline: Siegwave's remix, made as thanks for the song's message
cards.snippet: Producer Siegwave made this remix in 2022 to thank Kendrick for the song's message of acceptance, while admitting the writing is flawed. One listener: "this sounds good! i feel like they butchered the music or the ambience in the original"
